grading_system.evidence: In order to graduate from Lamoille Union High School, students are required to demonstrate proficiency in content areas as well as in transferable skills. ... Total Credits: 24

schedule.evidence: Students in grades 10, 11 & 12 commit to EPIC for a semester and will engage in the program for two blocks on either blue or gold days. Most course entries are 'Course Length: Semester' or 'Year'. The catalog does not state how many blocks a student takes per day or per term.

credit_definition.text: Not stated as a general rule. The catalog states that a semester two-block science experience (EPIC: Rewild) earns 1.0 credit; full-year and semester course entries carry no credit amount in the course descriptions.
credit_definition.evidence: Students can earn 1.0 credit of science in this 2-block experience. (EPIC: Rewild, a semester experience on blue or gold days). 0.5 per semester course is derived from that figure, not separately stated.

course_load.evidence: Schedules can be modified to incorporate traditional classes as well as the EPIC experience.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog states requirements directly in credits (English 4, Math 3, Science 3, Social Studies 3, PE 1.5, Art 1, Health 0.5, Capstone 0.5, Electives 7.5; total 24). No conversion needed.

cte_centers: Green Mountain Technology and Career Center (GMTCC)
notes: Local requirements beyond credits: demonstrated proficiency in content areas and transferable skills (p.3); Capstone Project 0.5 credit (Capstone Seminar course entry, p.27); Health half year required (p.29); half year/one semester of PE, Strength and Conditioning or Lifetime Fitness must be passed (p.30); Introduction to Dance can satisfy either the Art or PE requirement (p.17). Courses are listed as semester or year length; the catalog gives no courses-per-term count, so courses_per_term is null. Proficiency scores appear only as course prerequisites (e.g. 'proficiency of 2.6 or higher', p.16), with no stated scale or graduation threshold. The GMTCC section (p.4) lists full-day programs for juniors and seniors without credit amounts.
